questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Vilnius?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Lithuania is Vilnius.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Lithuania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Lithuania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: It borders Latvia to the north, Belarus to the southeast, Poland to the south and Russia to the southwest.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Lithuania about 65,300 square kilometres; Estonia about 45,335 square kilometres; Denmark about 42,925 square kilometres; Moldova about 33,844 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Lithuania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Lithuania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Lithuania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Overview” part of the Lithuania article.

questions.proof: Vilnius is the capital and largest city.
